CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ CardKeyword.Exhaust }` (ThinkingAhead.cs:14) == `self.exhausts = True`, set in `_init_vars` so `downgrade()` can undo the upgrade's `RemoveKeyword` -- the correct pattern, and `card_probes.py downgrade` does not list thinking_ahead.

ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (ThinkingAhead.cs:18-21) == cost 0 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new CardsVar(2)` (ThinkingAhead.cs:16) == `_cards = 2`, the number DRAWN (exactly one is then put back).

OnPlay.rationale: Order matches and it is the whole card: DRAW FIRST (`CardPileCmd.Draw(choiceContext, DynamicVars.Cards.BaseValue, Owner)`, ThinkingAhead.cs:25, == `DrawCmd.draw(ctx.player, self._cards)`), THEN select one hand card with a null filter and move it to the TOP of the draw pile (26-30 == `CardSelectCmd.from_hand(..., count=1)` then `hand.remove` + `draw_pile.append`, where end-of-list is the top by the sim's convention). Drawing before selecting is what lets the player put back one of the cards just drawn, and both sides do it. Thinking Ahead cannot select itself on either side (Play pile in C#, discard-pile limbo in the sim). BLAST RADIUS, not re-verdicted here per rule 3: `CardSelectCmd` auto-selects with no player choice and no RNG at or below MinSelect (CardSelectCmd.cs:287-290) where the sim's `select_cards` always delegates and otherwise falls back to `self._rng.sample` (combat.py:575-581) -- creature_card_cmds steps 104/105 and guard N10.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `RemoveKeyword(CardKeyword.Exhaust)` (ThinkingAhead.cs:35) == `self.exhausts = False`. The CARDS var stays 2 when upgraded on both sides.
